Subject: MAP & Eval acceptance protocol for pilot

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Avery's product team is enthusiastic about trying Redwood for our document summarization pipeline. Procurement asked me to get a concrete Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a short list of objective acceptance tests so we can align timelines with our security review.

High-level asks from our side:
- Pilot duration: 3 weeks (we can be flexible if MAP shows value early)
- Clear pass/fail acceptance tests tied to latency, accuracy (F1/recall on labeled set), and data handling assurances
- A simple rollout/takedown timeline and what support you will provide during the pilot

Could you send a MAP workbook and a recommended acceptance-test matrix by mid-week? We need that to feed into our vendor review on Friday.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Senior PM, Data Platforms
Avery Health

[Attachment: vendor_req_summary.pdf (1 page)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@averyhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & Eval acceptance protocol for pilot

Hi Emily — really appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass MAP workbook tailored for Avery (MAP_workbook_avery_v1.xlsx) plus a short security sample we use for procurement reviews. Key pieces in the workbook: 

1) Acceptance test matrix (objective):
   - Latency: 99th %-ile response under 450ms for up to 5 concurrent users (test harness included)
   - Quality: Macro F1 >= 0.78 on Avery labeled validation set (we included an evaluation harness and sample prompts)
   - Data handling: No customer data persisted in host cache; exportable audit log for all inference requests
   - Edge cases: Precision on PHI redaction rules — >95% recall on named-entity redaction test files

2) Exit gates (what fails the pilot):
   - Any two critical security issues from the intake questionnaire unresolved within 5 business days
   - Sustained 99th %-ile latency >750ms during normal load (30m window)
   - Quality metric regression of >0.08 compared to baseline on key prompt set

3) Acceptance tests (how we'll verify):
   - Daily smoke tests (automated): latency and token-level cost reports
   - End-of-week evaluation batch to compute F1 and regression vs. baseline
   - Manual review: 25 sampled outputs per week for PHI handling and hallucination review (shared doc for comments)

4) Timeline / responsibilities (proposal):
   - Week 0 (prep): onboarding, dataset drop-off (Avery), security questionnaire completion
   - Week 1 (canary): small traffic, validate latency targets, initial quality run
   - Week 2 (scale): increase concurrency, monitor regressions, run regression suite
   - Week 3 (finalize): acceptance tests, sign-off or deprovision

Action items for Emily / Avery:
- Drop labeled validation set + PHI redaction spec to the Drive link in the workbook by Wed EOD
- Confirm whether data must remain in-region (US-only) — if yes we will enable VPC-private mode for the pilot

We referenced a few optional controls (quantization profile, KV caching TTL) that impact both cost and latency; we called these out in the workbook with recommended settings for Avery's expected 10k monthly active documents.

Attachments: MAP_workbook_avery_v1.xlsx, security_sample_response_Q3.pdf

I'm happy to jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the team through the acceptance tests. Jordan / Marcus — flag anything you want tightened before I share this with procurement.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Direct: (415) 555-0127
[Attachment: MAP_workbook_avery_v1.xlsx (workbook)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & Eval acceptance protocol for pilot

Quick notes after reviewing Soojin's workbook — adding here so we have a single record before we iterate with Avery/procurement:

- Latency target: bump 99th %-ile target for scaled load to 500ms and add a canary window (first 24 hours at limited concurrency) before full Week 2 ramp. That keeps expectations realistic for their concurrent usage pattern.
- Security: add an explicit data-residency acceptance test if Avery mandates US-only storage (this is an all-or-nothing gate)
- Monitoring: add a pre-agreed SLI dashboard URL (we'll give read-only access) and a 30-minute on-call window for the final 48 hours of the pilot
- Rollback trigger: if any of the exit gates fire, we will automatically revert to a no-write-only mode and notify their SOC team within 1 hour

I'll update the workbook for these items unless you want to include them in the first revision we send to Emily.

-Jordan
Director, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
